First 12 rows of the test split (config 'default') via the HuggingFace datasets-server rows API. The translation script for this pack, versioned in this repository (builders/build_math_card.py) alongside the pack, so pack and builder land in one commit; earlier packs pin builders in the evalwarden repo instead. excluded.item: Solution (the worked solution per problem, including its final \boxed answer)
excluded.reason: Public in the dataset but harness-side: the sample target is derived from it (the last \boxed expression) and the agent never sees either. The integrity question is what the agent can see.

translation.notes: The agent prompt is the raw problem text wrapped in the task's prompt template (USER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE). The task loads the test split with shuffle=True and no seed, so the pack samples the first 12 rows in dataset order as a definition sample. The grader is modeled by its model-graded component (expression_equivalance); the two deterministic scorers are documented in the artifact's grader record and PROVENANCE (grader_modeling).

findings.title: Model judge has no labeled calibration set
findings.message: A model judge with no labeled calibration set is an unvalidated measurement instrument: its scores have no demonstrated relationship to human judgment. Unanchored rubrics and unpinned sampling temperature make the verdicts drift further without anyone noticing.
evidence: grader uses model judge the model under evaluation (expression_equivalance resolves get_model() with grader_model unset by default; -T grader_model can pin a different one) with no reference labels attached.
Judge scores are unvalidated against human judgment.
findings.remediation: Collect a labeled calibration set and report judge-vs-human agreement before trusting scores; anchor the rubric scale with explicit examples per level; pin temperature to 0 or take multiple repeats per item.

findings.title: Judge rubric has no explicit scale anchors
findings.message: A model judge with no labeled calibration set is an unvalidated measurement instrument: its scores have no demonstrated relationship to human judgment. Unanchored rubrics and unpinned sampling temperature make the verdicts drift further without anyone noticing.
evidence: judge rubric defines criteria but no anchored scale levels.
Without anchors, score meanings drift between runs and reviewers.
findings.remediation: Collect a labeled calibration set and report judge-vs-human agreement before trusting scores; anchor the rubric scale with explicit examples per level; pin temperature to 0 or take multiple repeats per item.

findings.title: Judge samples at temperature 0.5 with only 1 repeat(s)
findings.message: A model judge with no labeled calibration set is an unvalidated measurement instrument: its scores have no demonstrated relationship to human judgment. Unanchored rubrics and unpinned sampling temperature make the verdicts drift further without anyone noticing.
evidence: temperature=0.5, repeats=1: sampling noise can flip verdicts with no way to detect it.

runs_coverage_note: Definition-level card: no run records exist. Without runs, COST-002..004 and the attempt leg of GRAD-002 cannot fire; without judgments, trajectories, or repeated-run scores, JUDGE-003..009, TRAJ-001..002, NOISE-001..002, and DATA-001..003 stay silent, and GRAD-003 has no declared verifier rule or cached outputs to re-score. JUDGE-001 fires on the definition alone (it needs only the grader record); JUDGE-002 does not apply to the pointwise equivalence judgment. A definition-level card is a floor, not a ceiling.

canonicalization.applies_to: the generated card HTML, before sha256
canonicalization.rule: Two mechanical substitutions: (1) replace <footer>...</footer> with <footer></footer>; (2) replace the methodology-table Generated row timestamp cell with the literal TIMESTAMP. The harness version string is kept: the pack pins the exact version, so a version mismatch must fail, not be normalized away.
